Definition: evenness, i.e. (figuratively) prosperity or concord; also straightness, i.e. (figuratively) rectitude (only in plural with singular sense; often adverbially)
BiblicalUsage: The Lord judges the world in uprightness, the just man's way is uprightness, and the sons of men are asked whether they judge uprightly. The word is evenness, the straight and level path, and Scripture uses it for God's judgment and for the life that walks straight.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe uprightness is the shape of God's own justice: He weighs the path of the just, He judges the people in uprightness, and the straight way is the safe way. The straight way is the safe way, and the upright path is the one God weighs.
